  • Blog post: First Half 2026 Release: Agentic AI in SAP SuccessFactors Learning
  • Blog post: From Tracking to Acting: Strategic Insights from the SAP SuccessFactors Learning 1H 2026 Release
  • Video: Learning – SAP SuccessFactors 1H2026 Release (2:40 min.)

Employee Central Agents – Payroll and More

SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central brings you five new agents with the 1H2026 release, the first one for employees, the next three for the HR team, and the last one also for employees:

  1. Payroll Explanation Agent (for employees)
  2. Payroll Alert Resolution Agent
  3. Payroll Validation Rule Agent
  4. Employee Data Integration Agent
  5. Pending Workflow Agent

Payroll Explanation Agent

The Payroll Explanation Agent now takes time sheet data into account too. As an example, it can now answer questions which Alison has about the different overtime hours she worked on in January and February, as you can see in Figure 4. On the left you see that she starts by asking Joule to compare her last payslips, which were from January and February. Joule provides an overview of earnings and deductions along with a summary. When Alison asks “What are the different overtime hours I worked in those months?”, Joule explains how many hours were worked at a 1.5x rate and how many at a 2x rate.

Figure 4: Payroll Explanation Agent example. Alt Text: Three images showing how the chat conversation progresses, as described in the main text.

Payroll Alert Resolution Agent

This agent helps HR teams and managers to identify cases where an employees compensation deviates from the norm in some way – for example if their net pay is beyond a specified threshold value. It explains why the alert occurs, identifies the likely root causes, and recommends prioritized fixes. This makes it easier for less experience team members to deal correctly with issues, and also increases accuracy across the payroll process, resulting in up to 50% faster resolution of errors.

Payroll Validation Rule Agent

With this agent payroll administrators can use natural language to build new validation rules directly within the payroll control center, which are taken into account by the above Payroll Alert Resolution Agent. In the example shown in Figure 5, the administrator has asked “Create a validation rule for finding employees with overtime exceeding 20 hours in the period”, and Joule has created the rule with the help of the new agent.

Since users don’t have to go through technical configuration steps, they save up to 50% time for creating validation rules.

Figure 5: Payroll Validation Rule Agent example. Alt Text: image of a Joule conversation as described in the main text. At the bottom an illustration of a flag on a round hill is shown above the text “Validation Rule created successfully”.

Employee Data Integration Agent

This agent can cut the time it takes to resolve errors when employee data is replicated to SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central by around 20%. It translates complex technical error messages into easy to understand, actionable guidance. For example, if a cost center was missing, it would make a proposal for the most likely cost center to assign, based on the cost centers of the user’s peers who report to the same manager. Watch it in action in the video linked further below.

Pending Workflow Agent

If you are waiting for a worklow to be approved, but don’t know who the approvers are, the pending workflow agent can help. For example, if a manager is waiting for a promotion approval, the can tell the agent that they need it approved soon. The agent can then either remind the approver, or forward the request to their manager, depending on the approver’s availability.

Find out more and watch the first four agents in action in the first video, and the Pending Workflow Agent in the second one:

  • Video: Employee Central Payroll – SAP SuccessFactors 1H 2026 Release (3:49 min.)
  • Video: Employee Central – SAP SuccessFactors 1H 2026 Release (2:27 min.)

HR Service

The HR Service Agent in Enterprise Service Management helps users update data and create cases, for example if they want to report misconduct. Figure 6 shows an example where an employee wants to change their surname after getting married. The agent informs them that they don’t need to create a ticket for that, they can make the change directly – and helps them do it.

Figure 6: HR Service Agent – helping update data directly, avoiding a ticket. Alt Text: Three images showing the evolution of the Joule conversation as described in the main text.

Figure 7 shows an example of the flow when a user reports “I saw a colleague accept a gold watch from a customer – is that OK?”. The HR service agent checks company policy documents, explains that this is not compliant behavior. The user asks how to report this, and the agent assists and creates a case directly from the conversation.

Figure 7: HR Service Agent – creating a case for a compliance violation. Alt Text: Three images showing the evolution of the Joule conversation in full-screen mode as described in the main text.

Find out more and watch it in this video:

  • Enterprise Service Management - SAP SuccessFactors 1H 2026 Release.

Performance, Goals, and Career Development

Now that Alison has successfully started working and making a contribution to the team, the annual performance management cycle starts at her company. Time for her and her manager to agree on performance goals for the next year, as well as personal development goals, and for her to start thinking about how she might want to develop her career.

Goal Creation Agent for Performance Goals

Alison’s manager has asked her to make a proposal for her goals. Rather than staring at a blank sheet of paper, Alison uses the Goal Creation Agent to help her formulate performance goals. As you can see in Figure 8, the agent asks her for the main KPIs and tasks that she is accountable for. Rather than typing these in, Alison chooses to attach two PDF files: the strategy document and the team goals. The agent takes these as input for proposing her goals.

Figure 8: Goal Creation Agent example. Alt Text: Image of the home page with Joule on the right, showing the conversation outlined in the main text.

The goal creation agent helps managers and senior managers create goals too. The video linked further below shows an example for a manager leading a 113-person industries division.

Goal Creation Agent for Development Goals

Alison also needs to create some personal development goals. The Goal Creation Agent (also called the Development Goal Creation Agent) can help with these kind of goals too: she simply needs to describe in natural langauge what she would like to achieve, and the agent will make proposals, which she can edit as she sees fit.

Learn more here:

  • Learning: Using Generative AI in Development Goal Management
  • Documentation: AI-Assisted Development Goal Creation Based on Roles and Interests

Goal Progress Agent

Managers of larger teams can spend a lot of time following up on their team’s goal progress, for example:

  • Identifying whether everyone has set performance goals, and whether they are properly defined.
  • Identifying those team members who are at risk of missing their goals.

No longer! The Goal Progress Agent gives managers an overview of their team’s progress, and recommends actions to address issues, saving them a lot of time and effort. Figure 9 shows an example, where the manager asks “Assess the risk level for my team not completing their goals? Who is most at risk?”. In response, the agent provides an overal risk assessment, followed by a ranked “Most at Risk” list and a “Recommended Actions” list.

Figure 9: Goal Progress Agent – example Joule chat content. Alt Text: Two images showing the full-screen Joule conversation evolving as described in the main text.

Career Development Agent

Alison is interested in seeing how she can develop her career within the company. The new Career Development Agent helps her with this. Based on her current skills and competencies maintained in the system, it can recommend new roles for here, and also advise on the necessary personal development steps needed in order to grow into one of these roles.

Figure 10 shows an example, where the user first asks “What roles am I best suited for based on my skills?”. Joule provided three suggestions, indicating 59% readiness for the first one, “Digital Consultant”. When marking this role, a description of the role is shown on the right. Later, the user asks “Help me generate a development plan for my role”, and Joule shows the user’s current role portfolio, followed by a section “Strategic Priority Order” with a priority 1 role to aim for, with explanation of why, critical gaps and a detailed development strategy.

Figure 10: Career Development Agent – example Joule chat content. Alt Text: Two images with content as described in the main text. On the left the first ask and response is shown, on the right the second one.

Alison can use the recommendations from the Career Development Agent as input for formulating her development goals with the Development Goal Creation Agent described above.

See it in action here:

  • Video: 1H 2026 Release Highlights - SAP SuccessFactors Career Development Agent (1:04 min.)

Succession Planning Agent

Succession planning helps to build up talent pipelines, by ensuring that leaders and experts have potential successors identified. With this release, the new Succession Planning Agent helps managers and succession planners to identify succession risks and take action to identify and nominate suitable successors.

Have a look at an example in Figure 11. It shows extracts from a chat where a succession planners asks “Can you help me identify and prioritize positions for updating our succession plan this quarter”. Joule lists three positions needing attenction: a Senior Product Manager without a successor, a Lead Data Scientist with over-allocated successors, who have been nominated for other roles too, and a Regional Operations Director, show successor has inadequate readiness. The user chose “Action” for the Senior Product Manager, so Joule shows a list of suggested successors. The user chooses one, and Joule shows a summary of their experience, achievements, and strengths and growth potential. After choosing them as successor, Joule successfully nominates them.

Figure 11: Succession Planning Agent – example Joule chat content. Alt Text: Five screenshots of Joule showing the chat evolution as described in the main text.

Find out more here:

  • Video: 1H 2026 Release Highlights - SAP SuccessFactors Succession Planning Agent

More Information

Find out more about these agents here:

  • First Half 2026 Release: What’s New for SAP SuccessFactors Performance & Goals
  • Video: Talent Management - SAP SuccessFactors 1H 2026 Release (5:25 min.) – the Succession Planning Agent is shown from 1:59 onwards, the other three agents are shown from 3:44 onwards.

 

Additional Intelligent Insights

Giving people insights about their business data is a great way of improving the overall user experience: rather than having to go searching for information and compiling it yourself, you get relevant insights presented to you directly.

The 1H2026 brings these additions to People Intelligence, running on SAP Business Data Cloud:

  • Pay Transparency Insights
  • Compensation Planning Insights
  • Rewards and Recognition Insights
  • On-Boarding Insights
  • Time Management Insights

Pay transparency insights helps you analyze compensation across the workforce and identify pay gaps. In particular, it provides the required visibility for the EU Pay Transparency Directive, which addresses gender pay gaps.

Figure 12: Pay Transparency Insights –  compliance reporting of gender pay disparities (above), with drill-down to outlier analysis (below). Alt Text: Two screenshots, the upper one for compliance reporting, with a row of four KPI cards at the top, above two large cards contaning horizontal bar charts. The lower one shows Outlier Analysis for gender pay gap by worker category, with a clickable horizontal bar chart on the left showing pay difference between male and female workers per category, with “Administrative & Support Staff” selected; on the right a horizontal bar chart shows the coefficient impact on pay for different contributing factors, such as Performance Rating, Tenure, etc. At the bottom a list of workers for the selected categories is shown.

Look at more examples and read about how this helps ensure EU pay transparency compliance here:

  • SAP Introduces New Capabilities to Advance Pay Equity and Help Ensure EU Pay Transparency Compliance

Compensation Planning Insights and Rewards and Recognition Insights gives the HR team insights into compensation across the company, and how it breaks down to the various pay components, such as merit, bonus, stocks etc., plus insights into the kinds of awards (cash-based and points-based) that have been given. Figure 13 shows examples.

Figure 13: Compensation Planning Insights (on the left) and Rewards and Recognition Insights (on the right). Alt Text: Two screenshots, each with a row of KPI cards at the top, above various charts showing detailed insights.

Have a look at the above three People Insights in more detail:

  • Video: People Intelligence in SAP Business Data Cloud - 1H 2026 Release

 (2:43 min.)

On-Boarding Insights in People Intelligence provides insights on the progress and outcomes of on-boarding new hires, be they external or internal. You can see an example on page 13 of the

  • SAP SuccessFactors HCM 1H 2026 Release Highlights Brochure.

Time Management Insights brings together key absence metrics, trends, and performance indicators to surface absence patterns and their business impact, empowering HR to make data-driven decisions to improve resource planning and workforce strategy. Find out more here:

  • First Half 2026 Release: What’s new in SAP SuccessFactors solutions for workforce management

 

Enhanced Usability

In addition to the many AI agents supporting intent-based interactions, SuccessFactors has some areas where usability has been improved. I’d like to highlight these four, but there are many more improvements across the whole suite. Also, the next section on personalization includes aspects which directly enhance usability too.

  • Learning: the new Snack View
  • Integration of SmartRecruiters and SuccessFactors
  • Search for employees by skills, attributes and proficiency levels
  • New Enrollment Experience for Benefits

Learning: the new Snack View

When looking at your learning home page, you often see a row of cards representing courses for you to take. Now, with the new Snack View feature, you can get a quick overview, via a popover, of what the course is all about, without having to navigate to the full course details page. Figure 14 shows an example.

Figure 14: The Snack View in SAP SuccessFactors Learning. Alt Text: two screenshots, the upper one showing five cards representing available courses. It has an arrow from the third card to the lower screenshot, showing the popover with details: title, star rating, description, a chart indicating percent complete, and a list of associated skills shown in two rows of clickable buttons. Bottom right a “View Program” and a “Close” button are available.

Find out more about this and further innovations in SAP SuccessFactors Learning:

  • From Tracking to Acting: Strategic Insights from the SAP SuccessFactors Learning 1H 2026 Release

Integration of SmartRecruiters and SuccessFactors

We now have a much deeper integration of SmartRecruiters and SuccessFactors, providing AI‑powered recruiting via one unified experience with native integration that connects SmartRecruiters solutions, the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central solution, and the SAP SuccessFactors Onboarding solution. This provides a more consistent user experience across both products. It also provides greater operational efficiency via integrated navigation as well as by eliminating the need to manually enter data or replicate work. Single-sign on gives direct access without needing to log on, and automatic organizational data synchronization means that job families, cost centers and organization structures stay current across both systems. No manual clean-up is needed, since this avoids mismatched records.

Find out more:

  • 1H 2026 SmartRecruiters for SAP SuccessFactors: Connected Solutions and New AI-First Capabilities
  • Video: SmartRecruiters for SAP SuccessFactors | SAP SuccessFactors 1H 2026 Release (4:00 min.)

Search for employees by skills, attributes and proficiency levels

As so often, the details matter when it comes to usability. Now users can now search for employees by skills, attributes and proficiency levels directly from the enhanced People Search experience. This is a huge help for people looking to staff project, discover who has certain expertise, or for encouraging internal mobility. To use it, you need to have Growth Portfolio enabled.

New Enrollment Experience for Benefits

Employees can now manage their reimbursement benefits much more easily. A new, intuitive design makes it easy to enroll in, edit or opt-out of them. The new reimbursement enrollment experience supports all existing benefit types to ensure a smooth transition, see Figure 15 for an example.

Figure 15: New reimbursement benefits experience. Alt Text: screenshot showing details for Tuition Fee Reimbursement, with details and a list of attachments, and the right showing a side panel containing text with information on eligibility, covered expenses, and approve process.

US employees can now select their 401(k) plan from within SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Global Benefits.  A clear, configurable experience explains estimated employer contributions and guides them through deferrals and beneficiary setup, as you can see in Figure 16.

Figure 16: 401(k) enrollment experience for US employees. Alt Text: screenshot showing four sliders for selecting various contribution percentages and a field for entering the post-tax contribution amount. On the right a side panel contains text with information on “What is 401k?”, IRS Limits, and a pre-tax vs post-tax explanation.

You can find out more here:

  • First Half 2026 Release: What’s New in SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Global Benefits?

 

Design Updates for Suite Consistency

We have made design improvements which are relevant for a consistent user experience across the entire SAP Autonomous Suite, and which are now also available with SAP SuccessFactors. They include the shell bar, navigation panel, user menu, and settings dialog. These modern, standardized components are aligned to the broader SAP design system and provide greater consistency when navigating between SAP cloud solutions. Figure 17 shows the new navigation panel, which is opened via the icon to the left of the SAP logo in the shell bar.

Figure 17: Example of a personalized home page, with new shell bar and navigation panel. Alt Text: screenshot of the home page as described in the main text.

 

Personalization & Extensibility

Being able to adapt the system to fit your needs is an important aspect when aiming for an overall good user experience. Now, users can further personalize their home page, and admins can easily extend the solution to fit the company’s needs with the new extensibility wizard, integrated in SAP Business AI Platform (formerly SAP BTP).

Personalizing the Home Page

Users can now add up to five “Personal Quick Links” to the home page, so that they can directly access their favorite links. They can also now upload their own background images for  the greeting section, making it “their” start page. Figure 17 above shows an example, with a personal background image and these four personal quick links visible in the second row of quick links visible on the background image: “Gym schedule”, “Cafeteria Menus”, “Walkme Admin”, and “My Classes”.

Embedded Extensibility Wizard

The embedded extensibility wizard from SAP Business AI Platform brings a guided, in-application experience to create custom extensions in SuccessFactors HCM, whether adding a new data field, designing a UI card, or orchestrating a business process.

You can use it to extend People Profile, Spotlight, and the Home Page by creating UI cards that surface organization-specific data. Figure 18 shows an example where the user has chosen to create a highlight card as a user interface extension.

Figure 18: Embedded extensibility wizard. Alt Text: a popover “Create Extension” with a five-step guided procedure, showing step 5 “Summary”, with “Previous”, “Create”, and “Cancel” buttons.

Find out more in this video:

  • Video: Platform and System Administration - SAP SuccessFactors 1H 2026 Release (2:57 min.) The section on extensibility wizard starts at 0:28.

 

Enhanced Mobile UX

We continue to invest in providing a good mobile experience, and bring you these enhancements with the 1H2026 release:

  • Home page personalization and more
  • AI-assisted writing available, and further enhancements
  • Enhancements to SAP SuccessFactors app for Microsoft Teams

Home page personalization and more

You can now personalize Quick Actions and Quick Links on your mobile phone while on the go. In addition, the “Explore More” section is now fully supported on mobile, providing access to the same banners and analytic cards that are available on web.

AI-Assisted Writing Available, and Further Enhancements

Not everyone is great at formulating texts, an area where generative AI can help a lot. On mobile, you don’t want to be trying to copy paste text from your favorite AI-tool into an SAP application, so I’m pleased to say that we now embed AI-assisted writing directly into the SAP Success Factors mobile app. Whether adding goals, providing feedback, or creating a self-introduction in the People Profile, employees can receive tailored suggestions that make daily writing more impactful. Figure 19 shows an example.

Figure 19: AI-assisted writing on SAP SuccessFactors mobile app. Alt Text: Screenshot of “Edit Profile”, with a long text field “Introduct yourself briefly” shown at the bottom, with an AI button “Regenerate”.

Further enhancements: We are bringing several existing web experiences to mobile, enabling users to

  • easily create and track HR tickets,
  • view and rate skill proficiency levels,
  • manage work schedules, and
  • request temporary adjustments, and more.

Enhancements to SAP SuccessFactors app for Microsoft Teams

Employees can now easily complete more HR tasks directly within their flow of work using the enhancements we have made to the SAP SuccessFactors app for Microsoft Teams. In this release we have added:

  • Calendar sync notifications for absence changes, helping ensure schedules stay up to date when an absence is updated or cancelled.
  • The Clock My Time quick action now supports geofencing so that employees can use Microsoft Teams on a supported mobile device to record time when physically present in an approved location.
  • The Microsoft Teams app now supports onboarding notifications and HR ticket creation and tracking.

Find out more:

  • SAP SuccessFactors 1H 2026 Release: UX and Mobile Innovations

 

Further Information on 1H2026 Release Highlights

These four assets give you an overview of the overall release highlights for 1H2026, in increasing level of detail:

  • Video: SAP SuccessFactors HCM 1H 2026 Release Highlights (4:55 min.)
  • First Half 2026 Release: What’s New in SAP SuccessFactors HCM?
  • SAP SuccessFactors 1H 2026 Release: What’s New & What Matters
  • SAP SuccessFactors HCM 1H 2026 Release Highlights Brochure.

You can find detailed blog posts and videos for each are on our HCM innovations page, where you can scroll down to the section Learn more about our latest HCM innovations to see videos and blog posts covering the 1H2026 release innovations:

  • Human capital management innovations.

Finally, for all the details, have a look at the documentation:

  • SAP SuccessFactors What’s New Viewer.

entry.title: SAP UX Q3/2026 Update – Part 4: SAP Fieldglass
entry.content:
This fouth post in my series gives an overview of latest UX innovations in SAP Fieldglass, for managing your external workforce. Suppliers benefit from a brand new statement of work (SOW) dashboard, amongst other improvements. The latest release brings AI-assisted SOW worker role recommendations, for faster and consistent role assignments, as well as improvements to the home page and numerous further usability improvements in details that make a difference in day-to-day work. See for yourself!

In case you missed it, Part 1 of this series provides general updates about Joule, SAP Work Zone and SAP Mobile Start.

Also, if you haven’t already done so, do have a look at the many UX innovations which already came out with the SAP Fieldglass 2H2025 release:

  • SAP User Experience Q1/2026 Update – Part 6: SAP Fieldglass.

The topics will be presented in these sections:

Improvements for Suppliers
-  New Supplier Statement of Work (SOW) dashboard
-  View contract details
-  Easy navigation to SAP Business Network service entry sheet
Updated Home Page
-  Show job postings created for others
-  Unread message indicator
AI-assisted statement of work (SOW) worker role recommendations
Selected Usability Improvements
-  New grouping options on SOW events
-  Improved account category handling
-  Save draft for SOW
-  Quantity displayed in event itemization
-  Field updates highlighted on SOW revision
Further Information

 

Improvements for Suppliers

New Supplier Statement of Work (SOW) Dashboard

Hot on the heels of the new home page for suppliers that I featured in my previous post, which by the way has been redesigned to become even more intuitive, we now also provide suppliers with a statement of work (SOW) dashboard. This is a centralized portal that gives suppliers a unified, real-time view of all SOWs to streamline operations and improve program performance – Figure 1 shows an example.

The new dashboard:

  • Improves visibility for suppliers into their active and pending SOWs.
  • Streamlines collaboration between buyers and suppliers through shared insights.
  • Improves navigation and reduces manual tracking via external tools or communications.
  • Enables faster response times for SOW updates, approvals, and changes.
  • Provides greater accuracy and efficiency in managing deliverables, financials, and compliance.

Figure 1: Statement of work dashboard for suppliers. Alt Text: Screenshot of SOW dashboard with “My Group” selected, showing four cards with lists summarizing the number of critical and warning items per SOW for activity items, worker activity items, line items and upcoming worker end dates.

Find out more, and watch it in action:

  • Documentation: SOW Dashboard for Suppliers
  • Video: SOW Dashboard for Suppliers (1:11 min.)

View Contract Details

The 1H2026 also improves suppliers’ operational experience and provides real-time transparency into contracts. It comes with a new UI, provided by a new supplier admin object, allowing suppliers to view and download contract details (see Figure 2). These include key terms and rates, ensuring transparency and alignment during service delivery and charge submission.

Figure 2: New UI for suppliers to view and download contract details. Alt Text: screenshot showing maintenance contract details, a header form above a table with two items, and a “Download Data” button.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: View the Event Hierarchy Custom Lookup Data Maintained by Your Buyer Companies

This blog post summarizes the

  • Top 5 SAP Fieldglass Enhancements Every Supplier Should Know

Easy Navigation to SAP Business Network Service Entry Sheet

Suppliers’ users can now move directly from SOW events in SAP Fieldglass to the related Service Entry Sheet (SES) in SAP Business Network, simply by clicking on the new Business Network Workbench link in the event UI. Figure X shows an example. This simplifies access to required documentation and accelerates invoice completion in SAP Business Network.

Figure 3: Navigation enabled from itemized event in SAP Fieldglass to corresponding Service Entry Sheets (SES) in SAP Business Network. Alt Text: Screenshot of “Review Events” screen, with link to Business Network Workbench.

 

Updated Home Page

We have made some important updates to the home page for your employees: you have a new card which clearly distinguishes those job postings that you have created for yourself and those that you have created for others. Also, we provide an indicator in the messages tab to show that you have unread messages – so that new messages are brought to your attention.  

Show Job Postings Created for Others

As you can see on the right in Figure 4, the Job Postings card has two views, Created By Me and Created For Others, showing the list of job postings that you created either for yourself or for colleagues. This means that you get this overview at a glance, without having to navigate to separate sections.

Figure 4: Job postings created on behalf of others visible on home page. Alt Text: Screenshot of home page with two large cards, “My Workers” on the left, with a list of five, and “Job Postings” on the right, with buttons for the two views as described in the main text. “Created For Others” is selected, showing a table with two job postings.

Find out more:

  • My Job Postings Card and Dashboard Ownership Visibility Enhancements

Unread Message Indicator

I never get tired of pointing out that the details matter for a good user experience, and here is an example: we now provide an indicator in the Messages tab to show when you have unread messages. This is particularly helpful when you generally stay up-to-date with your messages, so that you usually have no unread ones, because then the indicator will appear the moment you get a new message.

Figure 5 below shows what it looks like: the mouse pointer is right next to the new indicator.

Figure 5: Unread message indicator. Alt Text: Screenshot of the home page, with the Messages tab showing “Messages (9)” followed by a small orange dot indicating unread messages.

AI-Assisted Statement of Work (SOW) Worker Role Recommendations

Creating SOWs often requires significant time and effort to manually define worker roles and assign them to appropriate sites. Also, it can be repetitive, and if you are working with similar SOWs or standard role structures it can be prone to inconsistencies.

Now, SAP Fieldglass makes this much easier with the help of AI. Simply press the new Recommend Roles button on the start screen for creating a role for a SOW and the system will generate role recommendations based on the specific details of the SOW. Each worker role suggestion includes a role title, responsibilities summary, and skill qualifications.

As you can see in Figure 6, the recommended roles appear in a pop-over, and you select the one you want to use in a first step. In the next step (not shown), you assign sites to the selected role.

Figure 6: AI-assisted SOW worker role recommendations. Alt Text: Two screenshots: top left the start screen with the AI Recommended Roles button next to the “Define this Role” button. Bottom right a pop-over above the screen showing the four-step guided procedure “Create Statement of Work”. The pop-over’s title is “Step 1: Select Worker Roles”, with a list of checkboxes and role names, starting with “Recommended Roles (14)” above five roles, with a scroll bar on the right.

This feature nicely complements the many generative AI features for enhancing descriptions that were introduced with the 2H2024 release.

Find out more in the documentation about these AI-assisted features:

  • AI-assisted SOW worker role recommendations
  • Generative AI Features for Enhancing Descriptions

 

Selected Usability Improvements

The 1H2026 release comes with some additional usability improvements:

  • New grouping options on SOW events
  • Improved account category handling
  • Save draft for SOW
  • Quantity displayed in event itemization
  • Field updates highlighted on SOW revision

New Grouping Options on SOW Events

There are often large numbers of purchase order lines on the SOW characteristics tab that can be hard to go through without any additional context.

The new expand/collapse option for SOW events solves this. As a result, users can clearly see charges within each purchase order line, making it easier to work with SOWs that have several levels of events. Figure 7 shows an example.

Users benefit because it:

  • Provides a cleaner interface by collapsing details when not needed.
  • Reduces scrolling effort when working with PO lines.
  • Improves usability by giving users control over how much detail is displayed.

Figure 7: New grouping options on SOW events. Alt Text: Screenshot showing a list of purchase order lines with three groups, the first two collapsed at top level, the third one expanded to level 3.

Groups are expanded by default and can be collapsed by choosing the arrow icon next to the parent event. Each level of the parent/child event hierarchy is collapsed and expanded separately.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: Collapsible Event Groups on SOW Characteristics Tab

Improved Account Category Handling

In this release, the account categories used in Event Hierarchy events have been aligned with those used in the SAP ERP backend, be this ECC or SAP S/4HANA. This ensures a consistent user experience across SAP systems. Account category handling is made easier with intuitive, standardized workflows that improve the user experience.

But that’s not all: we minimize misclassifications and the need for manual corrections by

  • enforcing ERP-standard account category behavior via improved logic and validations, and
  • by no longer permitting “Unknown (U)” account category for supplier submission.

Figure 8 shows an example, with the list of available categories shown in the upper screenshot, and the pop-over UI for adding or removing cost centers for the “Cross accounting Type (X)” shown in the lower one.

Figure 8: Improved account category handling in Event Hierarchy events. Alt Text: Two screenshots, top left step 1 “Setup” of “Create SOW”, with the section Cost Allocation showing the drop-down selection menu for Account Category. Bottom right the pop-over “Add or Remove Cost Centers”, with the account category “X” chosen, below that a table with input fields for searching for cost centers, and below that a table with two selected cost centers, and an Update and Cancel button.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: Account Category Management Alignment

Save Draft for SOW

This is another example of an improvement in a detail that makes a big difference in user satisfaction: users can now save a draft version of a statement of work (SOW) even if it has data validation error messages caused by incorrect or missing entries in input fields.

This means that they can interrupt their work at any time and return later to complete the SOW. Data integrity is still enforced when the SOW is submitted.

Figure 9 shows an example where the SOW has seven errors, four of which are displayed in the error message pop-over. At the bottom right the user now can select the Save Draft button, and resume their work sometime later.

Figure 9: Save draft for statement of work. Alt Text: Screenshot of step 6 “Review and Submit” of an SOW, with an error message pop-over showing 7 errors, and “Submit”, “Save Draft” and “Cancel” buttons.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: SOW Draft Creation Without Completing Mandatory Fields

Quantity Displayed in Event Itemization

Approving event itemizations from suppliers is now much easier and faster because we provide a configurable view of the consumed quantity for supplier charges, as shown in Figure 10.

This results in improved approval accuracy through direct visibility of consumed quantities, enabling more precise validation of work progress and helping prevent incorrect or inflated submissions.

It also provides a clearer, more meaningful view of actual work performed, critical for maintenance, engineering, and construction scenarios.

Figure 10: Quantity displayed in event itemization. Alt Text: Screenshot of “Your Work Items - Event” showing a table of five items with the Quantity column on the right highlighted.

Field Updates Highlighted on SOW Revision

When reviewing an updated statement of work before approving it, you want to know what changed since you last looked at it. This is exactly what this new feature provides: updated fields or sections, new or removed fields are highlighted in orange, with tables showing two columns for the new and current values if the current value has been changed. Only the latest differences between the current and the previous version are shown, in order to keep the view focused and intuitive. Figure 11 shows an example.

Figure 11: Recent changes in SOW pending approval are highlighted. Alt Text: Screenshot of part of the UI showing Accounting fields on the left and SOW Details on the right, with New and Current (if different) columns, and some lines highlighted in orange.

This enhances your user experience with clear, immediate visibility of what has changed, saving a lot of time by eliminating the need for manual version comparison.

It improves accuracy and confidence in reviewing document revisions.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: Field Updates Highlighted on SOW Revision

 

Further Information

For an overview of the major new features with the 2026.05 release, have a look at:

  • SAP Fieldglass 2026.05 Release - Spotlight Features Guide.

You can also watch the SAP Fieldglass 2026.05 Release Highlights video series. This series of 18 short, focused videos showcase some of the key innovations delivered in the release, with each video providing a quick overview and demo of the release item.

The videos have been grouped into four playlists, so you can easily choose which ones you want to watch:

  • Contingent Labor
  • Services Procurement
  • UX and Universal Updates
  • Supplier Updates

Have a look at all the latest updates, month by month, in the

  • What’s New Viewer for SAP Fieldglass.

Another good place to stay up to date is the SAP Fieldglass page on SAP Community.

 

Continue Reading

entry.title: SAP UX Q3/2026 Update – Part 5: SAP Concur
entry.content:
This fifth post in my series gives an overview of latest UX innovations in SAP Concur, for managing your travel and expense. The Joule Meeting Planning Agent is now even more powerful, able to flag big events taking place at locations which might spike hotel prices as well enabling you to block hotel rooms for attendees via the new Groupize integration. We are also introducing a number of powerful AI-assisted applications, such as the delegates dashboard or the approval manager, with AI embedded directly in the application – see for yourself!

In case you missed it, Part 1 of this series provides general updates about Joule, SAP Work Zone and SAP Mobile Start.

The Concur UX innovations are covered in these sections:

Joule: Meeting planning agent enhanced
AI-assisted applications
-  Delegates dashboard
-  Approval manager
-  Policy optimizer and benchmarking for administrators
-  Outlook: Corporate card management
-  Expense reports
Further information

 

Joule: Meeting Planning Agent Enhanced

This is a great example of how we are shifting away from a “click through the UI” user experience towards an intent-based experience, where you state what you want and the system figures it out for you.

The recently introduced meeting planning agent is already very helpful when organizing a meeting with participants from various locations: it helps you to identify the best location and hotels to minimize travel costs and book the travel (for example flights) and hotels all in one go.

Figure 1 gives you an idea of what this looks like, when the user asks “I’m planning an offsite October 20th-24th, 3 people coming from Seattle, 2 from New York, and 2 from Miami. Find me an optimal location near an SAP office that minimizes travel for everyone”. As you can see, the response lists suitable office locations and recommends best options, and then asks whether you would like to proceed exploring flight and hotel options.

Figure 1: Meeting Planning Agent. Alt Text: Screeshot of Joule with user prompt at the top and response below, as described in the main text.

Watch this video to get a better idea of the user interaction of what is generally available already today:

  • Video: Meeting Planning Agent

As announced a few days ago, we are significantly enhancing its capabilities.

From a UX perspective,

  • we are enhancing the shift in interaction model towards natural language, intent-based experiences, and
  • we are integrating and consolidating, giving users the power of two products in one unified experience.

Intent-based: Imagine you are organizing a large meeting, with participants from many locations. Instead of clicking through location, date, and budget filters, you describe what you need in plain language – "somewhere with hotels near the office and good local food, avoiding conference weeks" – and Joule interprets that into a destination recommendation, proactively flagging conflicts (such as local events that would spike rates) that a filter-based search wouldn't surface on its own. For example, hotels in Munich are much more expensive during the Octoberfest weeks, as were those of Football (Soccer) World Cup venues when matches were scheduled there.

Integrated and consolidated: Especially for larger events, you want to block hotel rooms for attendees, to ensure that rooms are available for them, and also to get preferential rates. Up until now that meant going into a separate system, but we are integrating Groupize hotel room blocking functionality directly into Concur, so users can use Joule for this too. This reduces context-switching – one less system for planners to reconcile, and one continuous flow for the traveler from group booking to individual selection.

Figure 2 shows the start of a conversation covering this, where an RFP (request for proposal) is being created for sending to the proposed hotels.

Figure 2: Example Joule conversation for booking a block of hotel rooms leveraging integration with Groupize. Alt Text: Two screenshots showing a full-screen Joule conversation. The user prompted “I need a hotel block for GBTA Chicago”, and Joule makes a proposal for an RFP draft, with a buffer each side of the dates. The user specifies “Keep the buffer, 4 star, walking distance”, and Joule proposes three hotels, showing them on a map and providing cards for each with price per person. The user selected on, and Joule refines the RFP.

What changed for the end user:

  • Conversational input replaces structured search filters – plan a meeting the way you'd describe it to a colleague, not the way a form asks for it.
  • The system proactively surfaces risk (rate spikes, availability conflicts) instead of requiring the planner to know to check for it.
  • Attendees get a self-service booking link within the group's negotiated rate, removing a manual handoff step that used to sit with the event organizer.

What changed for the workflow:

  • Group accommodation data lives in one system of record instead of two, removing a reconciliation step planners used to own.
  • Built on an agent-to-agent model between Joule and Groupize — the products interact directly rather than the user bridging them manually.

This functionality is planned to become available to Early Adopter Care customers very soon (in September) and is planned to become generally available in Q4 this year.

Further reading

  • SAP Concur Sets New Standard for What AI Can Do for Travel and Finance Teams
  • The Business Travel Magazine: SAP Concur solution streamlines meeting planning 
  • Business Travel News Europe — Groupize meetings get handshake with Concur

 

AI-Assisted Applications

Nothing beats a good UI if you need a quick overview of what’s going on – that’s why people love dashboards. However, when you need to make decisions based on what you are looking at, that’s where AI can come in handy! Let’s have a look at some cool examples from the latest Concur release – many of which starting via Early Adopter Care (EAC) programs

  • AI-assisted delegates dashboard (EAC)
  • AI-assisted approval manager (EAC)
  • Policy optimizer and benchmarking for administrators (EAC)
  • AI-assisted corporate card management (EAC)
  • AI-assisted expense reports

AI-Assisted Delegates Dashboard (EAC)

This new dashboard helps assistants of executives and other travelers get their work done much more easily, by bringing together information from three different places all into one unified workspace, covering approvals, bookings and expenses. The dashboard also surfaces a prioritized "what needs your attention" view on login, rather than requiring the assistant to go looking across tools.

This is best explained by looking at some examples of what the design looks like. Figure 3 shows the Overview page, with the list of today’s tasks on the left, a row of cards across the top showing urgent tasks, ongoing trips, planning activities and follow-up activities, a map next to the list of ongoing trips, and at the bottom a list of recent activities.

Figure 3: Design example of Delegates Dashboard, Overview tab. Alt Text: Image of the application as described in the main text.

Figure 4 shows the task view, with a row of cards across the top showing urgent tasks, ongoing trips, planning activities and follow-up activities above the overall list of tasks. To the right you see details for the selected task, related to a missing receipt, and how AI is recommending the next step.

Figure 4: Design example of Delegates Dashboard, Task tab. Alt Text: image of the application as described in the main text.

Finally, Figure 5 shows an example of the travel view, showing large cards each representing an upcoming trip.

Figure 5: Design example of Delegates Dashboard, Travel tab. Alt Text: image of the application as described in the main text.

The AI-assisted delegates dashboard is available to Early Adopter Care customers now, with general availability planned for Q3/2026.

AI-Assisted Approval Manager (EAC)

With the help of AI, approving expense reports becomes much easier. The new AI-assisted approval manager gives you recommendations for each expense report that is pending your approval. The approval decision itself gets AI reasoning shown inline (why something's flagged as risk, what the spend trend looks like), so the reviewer isn't leaving the approval screen to go and build that context themselves.

Figure 6 shows an example, with three reports pending approval. AI recommends that you approve the first one, that you review the second one closely, with a bullet-point list of reasons why, and the third one recommends sending back to the requestor, again with a bullet-point list of reasons why. On the right you see a section with spend insights, with a chart showing planned vs actual team spend over time, above a list of approved reports, with indicators where AI helped with the approval.

Figure 6: AI-assisted approval manager. Alt Text: image of the application as described in the main text.

The AI-assisted approval manager is available to Early Adopter Care customers now, with general availability planned for Q4/2026.

Policy Optimizer and Benchmarking for Administrators (EAC)

The new control center for expense administrators, first released in June, has some exciting new AI-assisted features to optimizing travel policies and benchmarking program performance against similar organizations.

Policy optimization allows users to upload policy documents and AI will identify gaps between documented policies and what is set up in the system, helping them keep programs optimized and compliant.

Figure 7 shows the design of an example, where you see the “For You Today” section containing cards with recommended actions for you. On the right you see the AI recommendation, on the same screen, so that you have all the information you need surfaced in one place.

Figure 7: Policy optimizer and benchmarking for administrators in the control center for expense administrators. Alt Text: image of the application as described in the main text.

This new capability is available to customers via the Early Adopter Care program, with general availability currently planned for Q1/2027.

Outlook: AI-Assisted Corporate Card Management (EAC)

Planned to become available soon for Early Adopter Care, and generally available later this year, AI-assisted corporate card management will simplify virtual card administration by using AI to generate card programs from your policy documents, allow you to create auto-approval rules using natural language, and streamline employee virtual card requests. 

In the past, setting up a card program for your organization meant digging through lengthy policy documents, looking for spend limits, and manually configuring complex rules. Soon you will be able to simply upload your company’s travel and expense policy, and corporate card management will generate a virtual card program aligned to your policy. Spending limits are defined, merchant category codes are mapped, and a policy template is created for you. All you have to do is review.

We are also incorporating intent-based user experience into this: you will be able to use natural language to define auto-approval rules for corporate cards, in a similar manner to that provided by the Meeting Planning Agent described above. Auto-approval rules mean that employees can get funds faster and you can reduce the workload for approvers – providing an improved experience for everyone!

Figure 8 gives you an idea of the steps that are automated when creatinga new card program: it shows the pop-over displayed once you have triggered the creation. In the example shown, “Parsing Document Structure” and “Extracting Spending Limits” has been completed, “Mapping Merchant Categories” is in progress, and the subsequent steps are shown as “Matching Employees to Templates” and “Configuring Approval Workflows”.

Figure 8: Planned AI-assisted corporate card management. Alt Text: image of the application as described in the main text.

AI-Assisted Expense Reports

I don’t know anyone who actually enjoys compiling expense reports from the various receipts and invoices that they have. Now, Concur automates this tedious task for you.

Joule now assembles and audits expense reports automatically, from receipt to compliance check, so you go from tedious data entry to a quick review-and-submit.

If you click on that, you’ll see the report as shown in Figure 10, with the “AI-assisted” link at the top. Clicking on that brings up the pop-over explaining “How this works”, listing the steps “Incoming expenses scanned”, “Related expenses added into report”, “Report details automatically populated”, and “You can review, modify, and submit”. It also explains “If something looks wrong” with an explanation that you can move expenses out, delete reports safely, since expenses will be moved to Available Expenses, and you can override fields that have been populated by our AI assistant.

entry.title: SAP UX Q3/2026 Update – Part 6: SAP LeanIX
entry.content:
Co-author: Laura Lezeu

This sixth post in my series gives an overview of the latest UX innovations in SAP LeanIX, for managing your enterprise architecture. You’ll see how we are shifting to intent-based UX, where you state your intent rather than clicking around on screens, and how we are infusing AI into your applications to assist you in getting better outcomes, more easily and more quickly. Highlights are the Enterprise Architecture Assistant, the AI assistant for building custom reports, AI-guided actionable architecture recommendations, and AI-assisted automations and calculations. Our new MCP server gives agents access to LeanIX, and the AI Agent Hub makes it easy to govern every AI asset in your enterprise.

In case you missed it, Part 1 of this series provides general updates about Joule, SAP Work Zone and SAP Mobile Start.

We’ve collected the UX innovations in these sections:

  • The shift in UX to intent-based UX, proactive insights, and workflow continuity
  • Answer your questions in seconds with the Enterprise Architecture Assistant
  • Create transformations utilizing the SAP LeanIX MCP Server
  • SAP AI Agent Hub: Govern every AI asset in your enterprise
  • Build custom reports with your AI assistant
  • AI-guided actionable Architecture Recommendations
  • Identify missing data on application fact sheets
  • Close the gap between architectural design and transformation execution
  • AI-Assisted Automations and Calculations: Create and troubleshoot faster

 

The Shift in UX to intent-based UX, proactive insights, and workflow continuity

Enterprise architecture has always evolved alongside the technologies it governs. The rise of AI is creating a different kind of pressure, not just a new asset class to manage, but a shift in what the discipline can do and who can participate in it. That is where our UX focus has been.

A thread running through this is the shift from expertise-dependent to intent-dependent access. Querying the workspace, building custom reports, configuring automations and calculations, these tasks no longer require technical skills or developer support. They require the ability to describe what you need.

A second thread is about where insight comes from. The workspace has historically been a tool you consult. We've been working on evolving the tool to surface these insights: flagging data quality gaps to the people who can fix them, highlighting improvement opportunities in the IT landscape, marking at-risk transformations before they become problems. The shift from reactive to proactive is gradual, but it is directional.

The third area is workflow continuity in target architecture planning. Designing a future state, connecting it to initiatives, and governing execution have until now involved manual bridging across steps and views. This release brings those into a single connected flow.

And cutting across all of it: the same discipline SAP LeanIX applies to application portfolios: inventory, lifecycle, governance, now extends to AI agents themselves. As organizations scale their AI deployments, that architectural layer is no longer optional.

 

Answer Your Questions in Seconds with the Enterprise Architecture Assistant

Getting answers about your architectural landscape has always involved too many steps: filter, export, cross-reference, repeat. The Enterprise Architecture Assistant in SAP LeanIX Enterprise Architecture Management removes that overhead.

Ask a question in plain language. Get a sourced answer in seconds.

Figure 1: Enterprise Architecture Assistant. Alt Text: two screenshots, the top one showing the start page of the EA Assistant, with three “Try asking” suggestions above the prompt input field. The bottom one shows the user has entered “Which applications are reaching end of life within the next 24 months”, followed by the anser in a two column table, listing four applications and their end-of-life date.

What it does for an Enterprise Architect:

  • Queries your inventory, connected Confluence pages, and workspace files in one go, without manual aggregation.
  • Understands your meta model, so results are contextually relevant, not just keyword matches.
  • Every answer is attributed to its source, so you can trace and trust what you're seeing.
  • Nothing changes in your workspace without your explicit approval.

What it means for the business:

  • Risk and lifecycle audits that used to take hours can be run as needed.
  • Data quality checks and rationalization analysis become ongoing, not periodic.
  • Faster architectural decisions with less analyst overhead.

Beyond querying, the assistant can do structural work: generate capability models, draft architecture decision records, and propose fact sheet updates based on a document you reference.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: Enterprise Architecture Assistant

 

Create Transformations with the SAP LeanIX MCP Server

The SAP LeanIX MCP server connects AI agents directly to the workspace data, enabling them to act on the architectural landscape rather than just read about it.

Figure 2: MCP Server available in Transformations Explorer. Alt Text: screenshot of the Transformations Explorer, with “Model Context Protocol” annotation and arrow to the left of the screenshot, pointing to the menu entry “Custom Transformation” on the left side of the screenshot.

For end users:

  • AI agents can query your transformation and milestone data without manual exports or copy-paste workflows.
  • Upcoming write capabilities mean you can create transformations, initiatives, and milestones through an AI assistant directly.

For the business:

  • Reduces manual overhead for routine architectural updates.
  • Accelerates the path from insight to action in transformation planning.
  • Positions the workspace as an active participant in AI-driven workflows, not just a data store.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: MCP Server

 

SAP AI Agent Hub: Govern Every AI Asset in Your Enterprise

AI agents are being deployed faster than anyone can track them. The result is a fragmented landscape where no one has a clear picture of what's running, what it touches, or whether it's safe. The SAP AI Agent Hub is built to fix that.

Video 1: AI Agent Hub (click on the image to start the video).

What it does for AI Centre of Excellence teams:

  • Automatically discovers agents, LLMs, and MCP servers across SAP, Microsoft, Google, AWS, Databricks, and ServiceNow, no manual cataloguing.
  • Gives every asset a structured record: classification, status, architecture decisions, AI risk rating, and compliance mappings.
  • Provides a formal verification workflow so nothing stays ungoverned.
  • Surfaces observability data at session level: goal completion rate, tool-call correctness, execution paths, and root-cause analysis.
  • Maps agents to the business units, roles, and skills they affect, via SAP SuccessFactors integration.

What it means for the business:

  • Visibility into AI agent sprawl before it becomes a compliance or risk problem.
  • A defensible governance record for every AI asset in your landscape, regardless of who built it or where it runs.
  • Faster rationalization decisions: you can see what agents actually do, how they perform, and what they touch.

Find out more on the

  • Product page: SAP AI Agent Hub

 

Build Custom Reports with Your AI Assistant

Building a custom report used to mean a ticket, a wait, and a developer. That dependency is gone.

Connect the SAP LeanIX MCP server to your IDE, link your preferred AI assistant and describe what you need in plain language. The assistant generates the code. You preview it against your live workspace data, refine it through follow-up prompts, and publish directly to your workspace.

Figure 3: Example of a custom report built using natural language input. Alt Text: Screenshot of the “Reports” view, showing business capabilities per organizational unit, with columns of capabilities for Australia, Brazil, etc.

For end users:

  • No coding required: describe the report you need and iterate conversationally.
  • Results reflect your actual workspace structure: reports are fully aware of your meta model configuration.

For the business:

  • Custom reporting on demand, without queuing development work or waiting on a sprint cycle.
  • Teams get the specific view of architectural data they need, when they need it.
  • Any workspace user can create and publish reports, scaling access beyond a single team.

 

AI-Guided Actionable Architecture Recommendations

Analysing your IT landscape for improvement opportunities is ongoing work: identifying where to reduce technical debt, where costs can be optimized, where the biggest risks sit. We worked on a capability that surfaces that guidance directly, without requiring you to build the analysis from scratch each time.

Figure 4: AI architecture recommendations. Alt Text: Screenshot showing Inventory view, with a section on the left “Insight Details”, and a section on the right “Recommended Steps”, with the second step being “Generate a survey for app owners to verify compatibility”. This step has been triggered, shown via a text box with “Thinking” and a list of actions already done by AI along with the next one.

For end users:

  • AI-generated recommendations highlight key areas for improvement in the IT landscape, so you spend time acting on insights rather than constructing them.
  • Recommendations are grounded in the actual workspace data, specific to your architecture, not generic best practices.

For the business:

  • Continuous architectural guidance without dedicated analysis cycles.
  • Earlier identification of risk and inefficiency, tied to concrete improvement areas.
  • Moves the workspace from a record system toward an active advisor for architectural decision-making.

This is the first set of AI-generated insights for SAP LeanIX, with scope and sophistication expanding over the course of the year.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: AI-Assisted Architecture Guidance

 

Identify Missing Data on Application Fact Sheets

Incomplete application data is one of the most common sources of poor architectural decisions. We now surface data quality gaps directly in the inventory, so the people responsible for fixing them see them without needing to run a separate analysis.

Figure 5: Missing data highlighted in fact sheet. Alt Text: Screenshot of the Inventory view, with four cards highlighted at the top in a “Data Quality Insights” section, showing the number of applications not assigned to any Organizations, to any Business Capabilities, with missing Descriptions, and missing Lifecycle.

For end users:

  • Four cards highlight applications missing a description, lifecycle, organization relation, or business capability relation.
  • Selecting a card filters the inventory to the exact applications that need attention, no manual cross-referencing required.

For the business:

  • Data quality issues are surfaced to application owners proactively, rather than discovered during audits or reviews.
  • Improves the reliability of architectural decisions that depend on application data.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: Data Quality Insights

 

Close the Gap between Architectural Design and Transformation Execution

Planning a target architecture involves more steps than most tools support end to end. SAP LeanIX Architecture and Road Map Planning has been updated across the full journey: from designing the future state, to defining a plan, to governing its execution.

Design and Decide

You can now design your target architecture in a dedicated diagram type. Starting from your existing as-is architecture, you add transformations using any transformation template and model the future state of your architectural landscape. You can switch between viewing the current state, the changes, and the target state.

Once your design is ready, a guided experience lets you assign transformations to existing or new initiatives in one workflow. You can also generate an AI-assisted architecture decision from the diagram, including a structured description of the planned changes and a list of affected fact sheets.

Figure 6: Example target architecture diagram for finance capability. Alt Text: Screenshot showing a visual editor with a canvas in the middle showing a Finance box, containing an “Accounting & Billing” and “Audit/Assurance/Legal” box, each with a number of functional boxes therein. The “SAP FI” box within “Accounting & Billing” has three arrows pointing to boxes “Australia”, “France”, “Spain” outside the Finance box.

Plan

In the transformations explorer, transformations originating from diagrams are visually marked so you can trace their source, move them between initiatives, set milestones, jump back to the diagram, and navigate directly to the roadmap report.

Figure 7: Transformations Explorer example. Alt Text: Screenshot showing a table with Initiatives, with the filter “By Affected Fact Sheet” chosen.

Govern

Once your plan is in place, the roadmap report provides an overview to track execution. It now supports visual milestone editing alongside a range of usability improvements, including zoom controls, exact dates on the timeline, currency formatting, and adjustable column widths. In the roadmap and any other report, the side panel now shows all transformations impacting a fact sheet, so you can review, execute, or edit them without leaving the report. The landscape report with the impact view shows which applications and IT components are affected by active initiatives and highlights at-risk transformations.

This is the first release of these target architecture planning capabilities, and we will continue building them out throughout 2026.

Figure 8: Example initiative roadmap. Alt Text: Screenshot of the top part of the Reports view screen, showing a roadmap in a Gantt chart visualization, with a parent entry “Cloud Transformation 2027” and Wave 1 and Wave 2 child entries.

 

AI-Assisted Automations and Calculations: Create and Troubleshoot Faster

Workspace admins who set up automations to keep data current or calculations to roll up metrics can now do both faster and with more visibility into what is running.

AI-Assisted Automations

Describe your workflow in plain English and get a fully configured automation, including triggers, conditions, and actions, ready to activate. The generated automation references your workspace meta model, so triggers and conditions use your actual fact sheet types, fields, and subscription roles. Every result is editable before you go live. For example: "When the lifecycle phase of an application fact sheet changes to End of Life, send an email to all subscribers."

When an automation fails, you now see exactly which action failed and why. The execution log shows the full run history and can be filtered by status, date, automation name, and fact sheet, plus a per-action timeline for every run.

Figure 9: AI-assisted automations. Alt Text: Screenshot of the Automations configuration screen, showing an entry “Tag Gold on Perfect Functional Suitability” showing a trigger and action for this. At the bottom an “Ask AI” field is shown with a prompt entry field containing the text “When functional fit is set to perfect on an application, add the tag Gold”. Below that the text “Steps generated. AI can make mistakes – review results”.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: AI-Assisted Automations

Calculations

Previously, configuring calculations required writing JavaScript. Now you can describe the metric or field logic you need and get a ready-to-run formula that accounts for your workspace's fact sheet types, fields, and relations. The generated code includes inline comments so you can verify the logic before activating. For example: "For business capability fact sheets, sum total cost of ownership across related applications that are in the active lifecycle phase."

The enhanced configurations for automations and calculations are part of base AI capabilities. They require signed AI terms and the activation of base AI capabilities, but not AI credits. The execution logs for automations and calculations are available in all workspaces.

Figure 10: AI-assisted calculations. Alt Text: Screenshot of a calculation Editing “Total cost of ownership”, with fields for Details and Target Field. At the bottom an “Code Generation with AI” field is shown with a prompt entry field containing the text “For business capability fact sheets, sum total cost of ownership across related applications that are in the active lifecycle phase”.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: AI-Assisted Calculations
